output.summary: The backlog growth is mainly a measurement-gaming effect of the 20-per-day close quota. Closes count reopens and splits, so agents solve prematurely, split tickets and pick quick wins. Reopens rose from 6% to 23%, split children from 240 to 3,710 a month, and duplicates from 410 to 2,770. First-contact demand rose only 4%, and Payroll accounts for a small share of the backlog. Capacity was flat and effort is not the issue. The exempt Billing pod stayed stable, and Team C's partial fix cut its reopens. The reopen-rate artifact is ruled out by the audit log. Engineering bug load is plausible but unquantified. Suspend the quota, adopt quality measures, and classify the aged tickets. Hiring and a tougher quota are not justified now.
